name: Live Skull
label: Homestead
lede: Two guitarists from San Francisco, three singers, one rented room in Gowanus, and a Boston singer who showed up in 1987 and turned a noise band into something that could sing.

eras.title: Two guitarists, no drummer, no place to stand
eras.text: Two San Francisco transplants build a band around twin guitars and three people sharing the vocals, in the same downtown scene as Sonic Youth and Swans.

years.src: Wikipedia: Live Skull · Trouser Press: Live Skull
years.h: Mark C. and Tom Paine start Live Skull in downtown New York
years.p: Both guitarists had played in a San Francisco band called Crop and moved east in 1980; drummer James Lo and bassist Marnie Greenholz completed the band.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says Crop also included brothers Ivan and Andrew Nahem, later of [[Swans|3285dc48-9505-469d-ad8a-bdf2d3dba632]]. The first Live Skull lineup had Julie Hair on vocals and Dan Braun on drums, but Lo and Greenholz took over quickly, and lead vocals were split three ways between Mark C., Greenholz and Paine.

Braun went on to play with Swans, appearing on their 1991 album Body to Body, Job to Job. Trouser Press files the band with the avant-noisy New York scene that also produced [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]], Lydia Lunch and Swans.

years.h: Live Skull EP: six songs, under 19 minutes
years.p: Recorded at Plaza Sound in New York in August 1983 and put out in 1984 on Massive Records as catalog number Fat 1.
years.xp: The band produced it themselves. Desire Records in France reissued it on CD and LP in 2013 with eight bonus tracks, including live recordings and unreleased material.

eras.title: Homestead takes the noise
eras.text: Two albums for Gerard Cosloy's label, the second cut at Martin Bisi's studio in Gowanus, and a live tape from CBGB.

years.src: Wikipedia: Bringing Home the Bait · Wikipedia: Homestead Records
years.h: Bringing Home the Bait is the first album, on Homestead
years.p: Twelve songs, 39 minutes, recorded in 1984 at Evergreen Studio in New York with the band producing.
years.xp:
It came out as Homestead HMS 022. Homestead was a sublabel of the Dutch East India distributor, run by [[Gerard Cosloy|b3c600d5-e1dd-4525-855d-6d4f950c3be6]] from 1984 to 1990. Wikipedia notes the label became known for poor communication with artists and for not paying royalties.

Desire Records reissued the album in France in 2013 with seven bonus tracks.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cloud One (album) · Wikipedia: Martin Bisi · Wikipedia: Live Skull
years.h: Cloud One is cut at Martin Bisi's B.C. Studio in Brooklyn
years.p: Recorded in fall 1985 in Gowanus, out in 1986 as Homestead HMS 056, with tighter song structures than the debut.
years.xp:
Bisi opened the studio in 1981 with Bill Laswell and Brian Eno, and it became the room where Live Skull, Sonic Youth and Swans all made records. The band would return there for Dusted and Positraction.

Desire Records reissued Cloud One in France in 2014, adding eight bonus tracks.

years.src: Wikipedia: Don't Get Any on You
years.h: A November night at CBGB becomes Don't Get Any on You
years.p: Ten tracks including "Debbie's Headache" and a six-minute cover of Curtis Mayfield's "Pusherman"; Homestead released it in 1987 as HMS 083.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the recording to a November 1986 show at CBGB. "Pusherman" also appears on the CD reissue of Dusted as a bonus track.

eras.title: Thalia Zedek takes the mic
eras.text: Boston singer Thalia Zedek arrives, a new drummer and later a new bassist follow, and the band makes its best-reviewed records and then stops.

years.src: Wikipedia: Uzi (band) · Thalia Zedek: media · Trouser Press: Live Skull
years.h: [[Thalia Zedek|a22a05de-b2e2-437c-91fc-df7b67ceb584]] joins after her Boston band Uzi falls apart
years.p: Uzi ended in 1987 after one EP; Zedek moved to New York as lead singer, and ex-Ruin drummer Richard Hutchins replaced James Lo.
years.xp:
Uzi's only record, the 1986 EP Sleep Asylum on Homestead, made the Village Voice's Pazz & Jop poll at No. 5. Mark C. says Live Skull had been playing Uzi tapes on the road, so when Zedek mentioned the band, his reaction was "You're Thalia Zedek!"

He describes her singing as talking, shouting and melody at once. Trouser Press calls her "the perfect sparkplug for Live Skull."

years.src: Wikipedia: Dusted (Live Skull album) · Wikipedia: Live Skull
years.h: Dusted: Zedek's first record with the band
years.p: Recorded at B.C. Studio in mid-1987, eleven songs in under 37 minutes; the New York Times' Robert Palmer put it on his 1987 ten best.
years.xp:
Wikipedia also lists it at No. 29 on Melody Maker's 1988 Albums of the Year. The album's "5-D" video later appeared on the Atavistic compilation Twelve O'Clock High.

Homestead's US release carried catalog number HMS 090.

years.src: Wikipedia: Snuffer (EP) · Trouser Press: Live Skull
years.h: Snuffer EP: six one-word titles, on Caroline
years.p: "Was," "Face," "Chair," "Step," "Word" and "Straw" were cut at B.C. Studio in January 1988 and released on Caroline Records.
years.xp: Trouser Press says the vocals were integrated "much better" by this record. The six songs were later added to the CD reissue of Positraction as bonus tracks.

years.big: "That whole album is basically one song."
years.src: Wikipedia: Positraction (album) · Thalia Zedek: media · Wikipedia: Live Skull
years.h: Positraction is out on Caroline, pushed by a bassist swap
years.p: Mark C. on the record, which Sonda Andersson, ex-Rat At Rat R, plays bass on after Greenholz left in 1988.
years.xp:
Mark C. adds that Zedek wrote the lyrics while going through a particular episode. Martin Bisi and the band co-produced at B.C. Studio; it runs 32 minutes. Wikipedia says Andersson is a cousin of composer [[Glenn Branca|7c0735b8-6444-47a3-a244-522fa7925834]].

Spin called it "a festering, appropriately black-colored slab of grinding, slash 'n' drone, East Village-trash-shit noisecluster rock."

years.src: Wikipedia: Live Skull · Wikipedia: Thalia Zedek
years.p: Wikipedia gives "sustained lack of commercial success" as the reason, with Tom Paine leaving music for film.
years.xp:
Paine later earned an MFA in film at the University of South Florida and writes about world cinema. Wikipedia's page on Thalia Zedek puts the split down to conflicts; the sources do not agree, so both are given.

Mark C. kept going in Spoiler, Int'l Shades (with ex-Sonic Youth drummer Bob Bert) and Outpost 13. Zedek headed for Boston and formed Come.

eras.title: Zedek's next band: Come
eras.text: Zedek teams up with Chris Brokaw in Boston and Come lands on Matador; Live Skull's story goes quiet for a quarter century.

years.src: Wikipedia: Come (American band) · Wikipedia: Chris Brokaw
years.h: Zedek and Chris Brokaw form Come; "Car" comes out on Sub Pop
years.p: Brokaw, ex-drummer of Codeine, switched to guitar; the seven-minute single was a Sub Pop Singles Club release.
years.xp: Zedek had known Brokaw since the mid-1980s. Wikipedia lists Sean O'Brien and Arthur Johnson as the other founders; the band formed in Boston in 1990.

years.src: Wikipedia: 11:11 (Come album) · Wikipedia: Come (American band) · Thalia Zedek: media
years.h: Come's 11:11 comes out on Matador after seven and a half days
years.p: Recorded in July 1992 at Fort Apache in Cambridge with Tim O'Heir and Carl Plaster; Wikipedia says Kurt Cobain, J Mascis and Bob Mould all endorsed the band.
years.xp:
The title came from the band repeatedly noticing the time on a digital clock. Chris Brokaw called it "a sort of superstitious mantra." Rolling Stone later called the record "one of Matador's defining records."

Mark C. says that watching Come at soundcheck, they held the room with one song.

years.src: Wikipedia: Come (American band) · Wikipedia: Thalia Zedek
years.h: Gently, Down the Stream is Come's last album for Matador
years.p: After it, Zedek and Brokaw went solo; her Been Here and Gone came out on Matador on July 31, 2001.
years.xp: Wikipedia's Come page says the band paused after 1998. Come played a two-song set at Boston's Middle East in November 2007, a full reunion at Spain's Tanned Tin Festival in November 2008, and toured for 11:11's 20th anniversary in May and June 2013. Zedek's own page dates Come's end to 2001.

eras.title: Back in the room where it started
eras.text: Reissues in France, a reunion at Bisi's studio, and three new albums from a band that had not made one since 1989.

years.src: Wikipedia: Bringing Home the Bait · Wikipedia: Cloud One (album) · Wikipedia: Live Skull (EP)
years.h: Desire Records reissues the first three Live Skull records
years.p: The French label put out Live Skull and Bringing Home the Bait in 2013 and Cloud One in 2014, each with bonus tracks.
years.xp: Each CD adds live cuts and unreleased songs: seven extras on Bait, eight on both Cloud One and the EP.

years.src: New York Music Daily: A Historic Marathon Weekend · Wikipedia: Live Skull
years.h: Mark C., Marnie Greenholz and Rich Hutchins play B.C. Studio again
years.p: The 35th anniversary of Martin Bisi's studio drew the trio back to the room where they recorded three albums.
years.xp: New York Music Daily called it the band's first public performance together since 1988, in the same space. Tom Paine was not there. Wikipedia describes the night as a semi-private "Recording of the Century" event where they played and recorded new songs.

years.src: Live Skull Bandcamp: Saturday Night Massacre · Wikipedia: Live Skull
years.h: Saturday Night Massacre: first new album in 30 years
years.p: Ten tracks on Bronson Recordings, with Zedek and Greenholz guesting; Kent Heine plays bass.
years.xp:
The band says its old horror imagery gave way to something plainer: in their words, "the facts are gory enough on their own." The Wire heard some of the "scuzzy energy" of the Reagan-era peak.

Dave Hollinghurst joined on guitar in 2019, and Dangerous Visions (2020) and Party Zero (2023) followed on the same label. Colyn Hunt replaced Heine on bass in 2024.
